subject: sampling bias with index of association

messages.author: e653eb797a0bfda9
messages.subject: sampling bias with index of association
parts:
Hello, 

I have been using poppr to calculate the index of association in large SNP dataset across two populations, specifically a wild and domestic population.

However, our sampling has been heavily biased toward the domestic population, so we have 14 wild and 200 domestic samples. 

To try and account for the sampling bias in calculating the index of association, I have tried to use rarefaction along with samp.ia(). 

The steps involved in the rarefaction are below:  
  • Sample all 14 wild and 14 random domestic samples
  • Perform samp.ia() of 1000 SNPs with 100 reps
  • Repeat this 100 times. 

The r loop I used for this is pasted below, where "domestic" and "wild" are simply vectors with the names of samples in each population.


### index of association using rarefaction

# create empty list to populate with loop
list_ia <- vector("list", 100)

for(i in 1:100) {
  
  # sample 14 random domestic samples
  domestic_sample <- sample(domestic, 14, replace = FALSE)
  
  # combine 14 random domestic and 14 wild into a vector
  selection <- c(domestic_sample, wild)  
  
  # filter genlight for sample selection 
  genlight_sample <- genlight[match(selection, indNames(genlight))]
  
  # ia
  sample_ia_wild     <- samp.ia(popsub(genlight_sample, "Wild"),     n.snp = 1000, reps = 100)
  sample_ia_domestic <- samp.ia(popsub(genlight_sample, "Domestic"), n.snp = 1000, reps = 100)
  
  # create df
  sample_ia_df <- data.frame(wild     = sample_ia_wild,
                             domestic = sample_ia_domestic)
  
  # add to list
  list_ia[[i]] <- sample_ia_df
  
  print(paste(i, "done"))
  
}

Using this approach I have found that ia stays relatively consistent for the wild population whereas ia varies for the domestic population in each iteration of the for loop depending on the sample selection (see boxplot-iteration-1-9 attached).

This is confirmed when I create boxplot of all iterations combined (see boxplots-combined).

Does this approach seem sensible considering the sampling bias? 

I am aware that poppr can do some interesting data shuffling (shufflepop) but I was unsure how to apply it for our data. 

Best wishes
Ollie

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: sampling bias with index of association
parts:
Yes, poppr does have data shuffling capabilities, but not for genlight objects, unfortunately.

The approach seems sensible. Another approach that I've seen work well is in figure 2 of Tabima et al 2018 (https://apsjournals.apsnet.org/doi/10.1094/MPMI-10-17-0258-R) where they compared the observed values of the index of association against simulated populations with different levels of linkage. One other thought: the nature of the spread in the domestic population may be due to the presence of missing data, which could result in lower values of the index.
